results.answer: Arizona statute defines land surveying practice to include measuring features 'in the air' and on the surface to determine location, topography, grades and contours and preparing maps of them; practicing or holding oneself out as qualified in a board-regulated profession without registration is a class 2 misdemeanor. Whether a plain (non-survey-grade) orthomosaic falls inside the definition is not stated; topographic/contour deliverables appear to.

facts.claim: A.R.S. 32-101 defines 'land surveying practice' to include measuring by angles, distances and elevations natural or artificial features in the air or on the earth's surface (Arizona).
facts.quote: Measuring by angles, distances and elevations natural or artificial features in the air

facts.claim: Under A.R.S. 32-101, that measurement is land surveying when for determining location, size, shape, topography, grades or contours, including preparing maps depicting these features.
facts.quote: maps depicting these features

facts.claim: Under A.R.S. 32-145, a person who practices, offers to practice or holds himself out as qualified in a board-regulated profession without registration is guilty of a class 2 misdemeanor (Arizona).
facts.quote: Practices, offers to practice or by any implication holds himself out as qualified to practice

results.notes: Search results (snippets only, not evidence) indicated AZ BTR enforcement against drone/aerial firms for unregistered land surveying (e.g. P16-041 Drone View Technologies, All In Aerial Solutions); those pages returned 403. Statute does not mention photogrammetry or orthomosaics by name; 'Mavic 3' equipment itself is not regulated.
